chunks: We have heard, O our Lord, the crier call inviting us to faith (and announcing): 'Believe in your Lord.' O our Lord, to faith we have come, so forgive our trespasses, deliver us from sin, and grant us (the glory of) death with the just.

key_terms.مُنَادِياً: a crier or caller who invites

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication of believers when they hear the call to faith?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited as the paradigmatic response of the faithful to the call of the Imams or the Prophet, highlighting the transition from hearing to active acceptance. It underscores the spiritual efficacy of sincere supplication (dua) in securing divine forgiveness and the ultimate reward of union with the righteous (al-abrar), a concept deeply linked to the Ahl al-Bayt in Shi'i tradition. The request for a good end (husn al-khatimah) reflects the belief that faith must be sustained until death to be fully realized.
